newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Underpined by samurai swap.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Underpined by samurai swap.

text.p: TCV NSW T-CORP QTC
OCT 98 7.16 (UNCH) FEB 98 7.03 (UNCH) JUL 99 7.33 (UNCH)
SAFA WATC TASCOR
MAR 98 7.10 (UNCH) APR 98 7.07 (UNCH) MAR 98 7.12 (UNCH)
*Semis slightly lagged Australian Treasury bonds in the past week after their recent outperformance, but expectations of more samurai issues seen preventing spreads widening too far.

Semi-government bonds slightly lagged Australian Treasury bonds in the past week after their recent outperformance, but the expectation of swap-related activity is expected to prevent spreads widening too far.

Last week's poor Japanese business survey killed off fears of a tightening in Japanese interest rates, keeping expectations high for further dual currency samurai bond issues to fulfil Japanese investors demand for high yielding debt, traders said.
"Pressure remains on the buy side," one semis trader said. "People who have been paying the swap to the Japanese on these new samurai issues are taking semis to cover that."

Long-dated semis yields, like those in the government bond market, were slightly higher on the week as Australian debt came under a corrective sell-off last week after the post-budget rally to 2-1/2 year yield lows.
However, Australian fundamentals remain positive amid a subdued inflation outlook and expectations that the Reserve Bank will ease monetary policy before year-end.

There is talk that the central bank will endorse an easing after Tuesday's board meeting, which is keeping the short-end firm, despite the backdrop of a weak U.S. bond market which is fearing a hike in interest rates by the Federal Reserve.
No domestic semis bond tenders are expected in the immediate future with Treasury Corp of Victoria and Queensland Treasury Corp having tapped the market last month.

Offshore, however, New South Wales Treasury Corp (T-Corp) tapped the Eurobond market last Friday with a A$100 million issue, paying a semi-annual 4.5 percent coupon and carrying a discounted 94.332 percent issue price.
The proceeds from the issue will be utilised to refinance existing state liabilities, currently being funded from non-domestic sources, T-Corp said.

An official for Nomura International, which lead managed the issue, said the bonds were aimed at the Japanese market and were finding interest due to continuing low Japanese interest rates and a perception that the yen would remain weak relative to the Australian dollar.
The discounted issue price gave investors some protection against possible current losses, he added.
The only other focal for the semis market in the near-term will be the Queensland budget on September 10.
